learningObjectives: Describe presynaptic release, cleft diffusion and postsynaptic receptor activation.
Differentiate ionotropic, metabotropic and electrical synapses.
Relate synaptic targets to medication effects and clinical symptoms.

anatomy.label: Presynaptic terminal
anatomy.detail: The terminal contains vesicles, active zones and voltage-gated calcium channels that couple an arriving spike to transmitter release.
anatomy.clinical: Botulinum toxin and several disease processes alter vesicle-release machinery.

anatomy.label: Calcium channels
anatomy.detail: Depolarisation opens presynaptic calcium channels. Local calcium concentration rises sharply and activates proteins that drive vesicle fusion.
anatomy.clinical: Small changes in calcium entry can substantially change release probability.

anatomy.label: Synaptic cleft
anatomy.detail: Released transmitter diffuses across a narrow extracellular space before reaching receptors.
anatomy.clinical: Diffusion is rapid, but transmitter clearance is essential to preserve timing and specificity.

anatomy.label: Postsynaptic receptors
anatomy.detail: Ionotropic receptors directly gate channels; metabotropic receptors activate slower intracellular signalling cascades.
anatomy.clinical: The same transmitter can produce different effects through different receptor subtypes.

anatomy.label: Clearance systems
anatomy.detail: Transporters, enzymes and diffusion remove transmitter from the cleft and recycle components.
anatomy.clinical: Transporter blockade is a major mechanism of antidepressants and stimulants.

interaction.title: Synapses sequence
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence to see how the system changes over time.

stages.label: Arrive
stages.text: An action potential depolarises the presynaptic terminal.

stages.label: Release
stages.text: Calcium entry triggers vesicle fusion and transmitter release.

stages.label: Clear
stages.text: Transporters, enzymes and diffusion terminate the signal.

quizBank.question: What directly triggers synaptic vesicle fusion?
quizBank.explanation: Calcium entering through voltage-gated channels activates fusion machinery.

quizBank.question: Ionotropic receptors differ from metabotropic receptors because ionotropic receptors:
options: Are located only in the nucleus
quizBank.explanation: Ionotropic receptors rapidly alter conductance by directly gating channels.

quizBank.question: What is spatial summation?
options: Inputs from different synapses combine at the same time
One synapse fires repeatedly over time
A spike grows larger down the axon
quizBank.explanation: Spatial summation combines simultaneous inputs arriving at different locations.

quizBank.question: Which process can terminate synaptic signalling?
quizBank.explanation: Several clearance mechanisms limit transmitter action.

quizBank.question: Electrical synapses transmit signals through:
quizBank.explanation: Gap junction channels allow direct current flow between cells.
